newsitem.title: USA: Daschle says most Democrats support US budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Daschle says most Democrats support US budget pact.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday that most Democrats would support an agreement on legislation to balance the budget and cut taxes over five years.

A tentative agreement on budget and tax legislation was reached Monday evening between congressional Republican leaders and White House officials. The bills are expected to go before Congress for a vote this week.
"An overwhelming majority of Democrats will support this agreement," Daschle of South Dakota told reporters.
"The bottom line is we will achieve balance on or before the year 2002 as a result of these two reconciliation bills," Daschle said.

He said he had spoken to leading Democrats on the House Ways and Means Committee and Democrats in the Senate. "My impression is given what I've seen overnight and the conversations that I have had, especially with my colleagues, that there is broad support for this in Democratic caucuses," he said.
